I wrote `src/index.ts` and `npm run build` finished with no errors (exit 0).

The contract is a single function. `reverseMapDiff(diff, table)` takes the diff text and the name table. It returns the mapped diff and a list of unmapped paths, each listed once in the order they first appear. A name table entry has a `kind` (`"path"` or `"identifier"`), a `real` name and a `public` name.

- **No errors:** the spec never says a call fails, so nothing is documented as throwing.
- **No environment inputs:** the result depends only on the diff and the table, so time, keys and randomness don't come into it.
- **Left to the implementation:** I didn't add any rules beyond the spec. One example is whether `/dev/null` counts as unmapped. The spec only says it is left as it is.

The build also produced `src/index.js`. I deleted it so `src/index.ts` is the only file written; it's gitignored anyway and the build will recreate it.

Exports: `NameKind`, `NameEntry`, `NameTable`, `ReverseMapResult`, `reverseMapDiff`

public.finalText:
I've written the public test suite in `tests/public/`, with two tests for each of the eight scenarios in the spec: the happy path and one boundary case. `npm run build` reports no errors. All 16 tests fail when run, as expected, because the function bodies throw `not implemented`.

| Scenario | Happy path | Boundary case |
|---|---|---|
| File headers mapped | All header lines map `ledger/sheet.ts` → `billing/invoice.ts` | `ledger/sheet.tsx` is not mapped and is reported unmapped |
| Directory entry | `ledger/a/b.ts` → `billing/a/b.ts` | `ledgers/x.ts` is not mapped and is reported |
| Hunk content | The spec's hunk, with the `@@` numbers unchanged and the text after `@@` mapped | `MySheet`, `SheetList` and `Sheets` are left alone; `Sheet` at the start or end of a line is mapped |
| Renames, new and deleted files | `rename from` / `rename to` lines mapped | `--- /dev/null` and `+++ /dev/null` are kept |
| Most specific entry wins | `ledger/core.ts` → `payments/core.ts` | Same result with the table order reversed; a sibling file still uses the directory entry |
| One pass | `+Beta(Gamma)` → `+Alpha(Beta)` | The result doesn't depend on table order |
| Everything else unchanged | Index line, whitespace, `\ No newline at end of file` markers and a missing final newline are kept | Mixed CRLF and LF endings are kept on mapped and unmapped lines |
| Unmapped paths | `docs/readme.md` is left as is and reported once | Reported in order of first appearance, with mapped paths skipped |

Where the spec doesn't say what should happen, the tests make no assertion:
- **`/dev/null`:** whether it counts as an unmapped path.
- **Identifier entries in header paths:** whether they apply there. The test paths avoid identifier names.
- **Path entries inside hunk text:** whether they apply there.
- **Identifier-only tests:** they don't check the `unmapped` list.

The build writes compiled `.js` files next to the sources, including `src/index.js`. I deleted them so that nothing is left outside `tests/public/`. Running `npm test` will create them again.

16 tests, in 4 files.

open: `new and deleted files: /dev/null headers are left as they are`: this test leaves it open whether `/dev/null` appears in `unmapped`, and the spec doesn't say either. The public test doesn't assert it, and I don't either.
